questions.prompt: On Sami's treasure map, the old well is north of the palm tree. Complete: "The palm tree is ___ of the old well."

options.text: west
north
south
east

questions.explanation: North is the top of the map, so the well is above the palm tree and the palm tree is below it: the palm tree is south of the old well. North would put the tree above the well, and east and west are the right and left sides of the map, which the sentence about the well does not use.

questions.prompt: A traveller arrives in New Zealand and visits a Maori family for the first time. How do the hosts greet him?

options.text: A warm handshake.
A kiss on each cheek.
A bow from the waist.
A touch of the noses.

questions.explanation: A good traveller meets the greeting of the country he is in, and the Maori of New Zealand greet each other by touching noses and foreheads gently. The handshake belongs to England and the USA, the kiss on each cheek to Tunisia, France and Spain, and the bow to Japan.

questions.prompt: A boat is slow, a train is fast and a plane is very fast. Which sentence is correct?

options.text: A boat is the slowest of the three.
A boat is slowest of the three.
A boat is the most slow of the three.
A boat is the slower of the three.

questions.explanation: Three means of transport make a whole group, and the slowest of a group takes the in front and -est behind: the boat is the slowest of the three. The ending -est never drops its the, a short adjective never takes most in front of it, and -er belongs to two things compared.

questions.prompt: The pyramids are about 4500 years old, the amphitheatre of El Jem about 1800 years old, and Big Ben was finished in 1859. Which sentence is true?

options.text: Big Ben is the oldest of the three.
The amphitheatre of El Jem is older than the pyramids.
The amphitheatre of El Jem is the oldest of the three.
The pyramids are the oldest of the three.

questions.explanation: 4500 years is more than 1800 years and far more than the age of a monument finished in 1859, so the pyramids stand first in the group and take the superlative: the pyramids are the oldest of the three. The amphitheatre of El Jem comes second, and Big Ben, the youngest of them, comes last.

questions.prompt: Complete with the adjective nice: "The small town was ___ the big city."

options.text: more nice than
nicer than
nicest than
the nicest of

questions.explanation: Two places are compared, so the adjective takes the comparative, and because nice already ends in -e it adds only -r: nicer than. A short English adjective refuses more, and the ending -est needs a whole group and never takes than behind it.

questions.prompt: Read: "Sonia prefers travelling by train. Last summer she travelled to Spain. There she watched a flamenco dancer and ate paella with seafood." Which sentence is true?

options.text: Sonia ate a rice dish in Spain.
Sonia prefers to travel by plane.
Sonia travelled to Spain by plane.
Sonia watched a bull fight in Spain.

questions.explanation: Paella is the Spanish dish of rice with seafood, and the text says she ate it, so a rice dish eaten in Spain is the true sentence. The text gives the train as what she prefers and never names the plane, and it puts a flamenco dancer in front of her, not a bull fight.
